findings.title: Backup code login can skip the password
findings.body: Password verification only runs when `user.password && !credentials.totpCode`. The new branch then accepts a backup code whenever `credentials.backupCode` is non-empty and never checks the password itself. The login UI clears `totpCode` before submitting a backup code so the password gate runs, but the credentials callback does not enforce that pairing. A caller who knows a backup code can send the victim's email, any non-empty `totpCode`, and that backup code and receive a session without the password. Backup codes are long-lived and typically stored in a downloaded text file, so this makes them a single factor rather than a replacement for the authenticator. Disable 2FA already requires the password independently of the second factor; login should do the same before accepting a backup code.

findings.title: Consuming a backup code is a lost update
findings.body: A valid backup code is invalidated by reading the decrypted list, setting that index to null, and writing the whole blob back with a plain `user.update`. There is no transaction, row lock, or compare-and-swap on the previous ciphertext. Two overlapping logins (double submit, retry, or two devices) both read the same list. If they use the same code, both pass `indexOf` before either write and both sessions are created, so the code is not single-use. If they use different codes, the later write restores the code the earlier request nulled, so a spent code works again. Consumption needs to be serialized, for example by locking the user row and updating only if `backupCodes` is still the value that was read.

findings.title: Dismissing the codes dialog loses the only copy
findings.body: After TOTP enable succeeds, the modal only advances to DisplayBackupCodes; `onEnable()` runs solely from the Close button. The dialog is still closed through `onOpenChange` (Escape, overlay, header close), which does not call `onEnable()` or `resetState()`. Codes are returned once from setup and kept only in component state. Setup refuses to run again once `twoFactorEnabled` is true, and nothing in this PR can list or regenerate them. Dismissing the dialog therefore drops the only display of the codes and can leave the settings page thinking 2FA is still off, so a later enable attempt hits TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled. The new `missing_backup_codes` string says to generate codes in settings, but no such screen exists, including for users who enabled 2FA before this column was added and have null `backupCodes`.

findings.title: Backup-code download click does not reliably download
findings.body: The download action is a `<Button>` nested inside `<a download href={backupCodesUrl}>`, which is invalid HTML (interactive content inside an anchor). The button handles the click, so the anchor's download navigation often never runs and `cal-backup-codes.txt` is not saved. Unlike the Copy and Close buttons in the same footer, this control also does not call `preventDefault`. It sits inside the enable `<Form>`, so if the button submits, the click re-invokes `handleEnable` with the already-used TOTP code instead of downloading. The new e2e test waits on a download from that test id and will fail or flake for the same reason.

findings.title: OAuth/SAML second-factor screen cannot use backup codes
findings.body: Lost access is only rendered in `TwoFactorFooter`. When login is reached with a `totp` query JWT (`totpEmail` set), the footer is `ExternalTotpFooter`, which is only Cancel, so those users never see the backup-code field. That is the path `loginWithTotp` uses after Google/SAML sign-in for an account with `twoFactorEnabled` (including CAL users whose password was cleared when the identity provider was linked). Even a direct credentials call with only a backup code fails first: `authorize` throws `ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled` when `identityProvider !== CAL` and `totpCode` is empty, before the backup-code branch. Those users still cannot get in with a backup code if they lose the authenticator.

findings.title: Copy toast reports success even when clipboard write fails
findings.body: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` is not awaited and has no catch, and `showToast(t("backup_codes_copied"), "success")` runs immediately. `writeText` rejects when clipboard permission is denied or the page is not allowed to write the clipboard, which is common in embedded or non-secure contexts. The user is told the codes were copied, then Close is the path that finishes setup. Because codes cannot be fetched again after 2FA is enabled, a failed copy plus close leaves them with no saved codes. The e2e test only waits for `toast-success`, so it passes even when nothing was copied.

findings.title: Backup code match does not normalize case or whitespace
findings.body: Stored codes are lowercase hex from `randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`, shown as `xxxxx-xxxxx`. Login and disable only do `replaceAll("-", "")` and then `indexOf`, so they are case-sensitive and do not trim. The backup-code input placeholder is `XXXXX-XXXXX`, which tells users to type uppercase. A code typed that way, or pasted with a trailing newline or space from the downloaded file, does not match and is rejected as incorrect even though it is the right code. The same comparison is in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` around the `replaceAll` call, so disable has the same failure.

findings.title: Tests never log in with a backup code, and enable flow is unfinished
findings.body: The new step shows backup codes and does not call `onEnable()` until Close, but the "enable 2FA and login using 2FA" test never clicks `backup-codes-close`. It still asserts the switch via `locator.isChecked()`, which this PR notes passes even when the switch is not checked, so the test can stay green if the post-enable UI never updates. The other test only checks download filename, a success toast, and close. Nothing submits a backup code at login, checks that a used code is rejected, or disables 2FA with a backup code. The file's own TODO calls that out, and the PR checklist says tests that prove the feature were not added. The password-skip and single-use bugs above would not be caught.
